President Biden believes that artificial intelligence is one of the most powerful tools of our time – but knows that to seize its opportunities, we must first mitigate its risks.

In 2023, President Biden issued a sweeping Executive Order on AI to ensure that America leads the way toward responsible AI innovation. The Executive Order takes a comprehensive approach to America’s global leadership in AI, encourages responsible innovation, and promotes competition. It also ensures that as new technologies rapidly evolve, the government continues to protect Americans’ privacy, advance equity and civil rights, and stand up for consumers, patients, students, and workers.

Additionally, thanks to President Biden’s leadership, 16 companies have made voluntary commitments on safe and responsible AI use. These commitments include internal and external security testing before releasing AI systems, sharing information with the public about safety risks and dangerous capabilities, and deploying AI to help address society’s greatest challenges.

When President Biden took office, the number of drug overdose deaths was increasing by more than 30% year over year. Because of increased funding and resources, overdose deaths decreased 17% year-over-year in the 12 months ending in July 2024.

Our Administration took critical steps to achieve this decrease – including seizing more fentanyl at the border, arresting and prosecuting dozens of high-level drug traffickers and cartel leaders, sanctioning over 300 entities and individuals involved in the global illicit drug trade, and forging historic counternarcotics cooperation with China.

Our Administration also expanded access to naloxone and other life-saving interventions, including working with Congress to remove barriers that prevented medical professionals from prescribing treatment for opioid use disorder.

tweets.text:
President Biden ran for office to restore the soul of our nation – and he has been clear that hate, bigotry, and violence have no place here in the U.S. 
 
That’s why our Administration has taken numerous steps to counter hate in all its forms. In 2021, President Biden signed into law the COVID-19 Hate Crimes Act, which includes the Khalid Jabara and Heather Heyer NO HATE Act, to improve the reporting and prevention of hate crimes and ensure that hate crimes information is more accessible to Asian American and Pacific Islander Communities. Attorney General Merrick Garland also appointed the Justice Department’s first-ever Anti-Hate Crimes Resources Coordinator and designated staff to oversee expedited review of hate crimes. And, the Federal Bureau of Investigation has elevated hate crimes and criminal civil rights violations to its highest-level national threat priority.
 
In 2022, President Biden hosted the first-ever White House United We Stand Summit to address hate-fueled violence and put forward a shared vision for working toward a more united America. At the Summit, President Biden announced the White House Initiative to Counter Hate-Motivated Violence to address violence and bias against all communities.
 
President Biden also established an interagency group to increase and better coordinate federal efforts to counter Antisemitism, Islamophobia, and related forms of bias and discrimination within the U.S. In 2023, amidst a historic increase in antisemitic incidents, President Biden released the first-ever U.S. National Strategy to Counter Antisemitism. In 2024, he released the first-ever U.S. National Strategy to Counter Islamophobia and Anti-Arab Hate.
 
The power is within each of us to rise together against hate and build a nation that treats everyone with dignity and respect.
